sections.what_happened: [ANALYSIS -- ISW (T3, ANALYSIS), Iran Update Nov 6] The Ansar Allah may be concentrating forces and materiel in al Turbah, astride the Taiz-Aden ground line of communication, in preparation for a large-scale offensive into Lahij Governorate and toward Aden. The Ansar Allah-controlled Humanitarian Operations Coordination Center (HOCC) has issued voluntary 'transit permits' in recent months granting civilian vessels safe passage through Bab el-Mandeb; the permit system sets conditions for the Ansar Allah to exert greater control over maritime traffic by normalizing their regulation of the waterway, closely resembling Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority (est. May 2026, for Hormuz). The Ansar Allah could at any time make permits mandatory and enforce it by striking vessels that refuse. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- WSJ Nov 6, recorded 0100-01] Ship captains email clearances@hocc.gov.ye; the Ansar Allah typically reply within 24 hours; example: the Chinese container ship Zhong Cheng Chang Ling's Sept 7 transit. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- Yonhap via Korea Herald, Nov 7] The Ansar Allah have demanded $51 billion in compensation from Saudi Arabia in negotiations, citing airstrike damage and the blockade. [PORTWATCH -- STALE] Newest IMF PortWatch snapshot remains portwatch-2026-10-26.json, stale=true, latest observation 2026-10-18: Bab el-Mandeb 32 transits that day, 7-day avg 26.4 vs 2025 baseline 33.5/day (79% of baseline). No fresh counted figure exists; none is cited as live.
sections.what_verified: 2 distinct tiered publisher families: Wall Street Journal (T2) for the HOCC email system; ISW (T3, ANALYSIS) for the al Turbah assessment and the permit-system framing. Economic Times, Korea Herald, Izvestia, Maritime Gateway, CrisisBrief have NO declared tier in the registry and do not count (attribution only).
sections.what_disputed: Marine insurer Skuld: the HOCC has no internationally recognised authority to impose transit conditions. Yemen's Maritime Affairs Authority (Aden), via GAC, urges vessels NOT to engage with the HOCC, citing legal, sanctions and security risks, and directs them to UKMTO/MSCIO. JMIC: Ansar Allah targeting does not follow a consistent or predictable method; a HOCC reply is not a security guarantee. On the Taiz market attack (30 killed, recorded 0100-02): Taiz authorities deny any airstrikes occurred and blame the Ansar Allah; AP could not independently verify either account.
sections.why_matters: Ships now email the Ansar Allah for permission to cross the Red Sea -- and the Ansar Allah are massing forces for a push on Aden while demanding $51 billion from Riyadh.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE TO totw-20261107-0100-01 (Ansar Allah HOCC email transit permits) -- ISW Nov 6: Ansar Allah may be concentrating forces in al Turbah for a large-scale offensive toward Aden; HOCC permit system normalizing control of Bab el-Mandeb; $51bn reparations demand from Saudi Arabia

totw_analysis: Our read: Ships now email the Ansar Allah for permission to cross the Red Sea -- and the Ansar Allah are massing forces for a push on Aden while demanding $51 billion from Riyadh. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Are the Ansar Allah becoming the Red Sea's toll collectors -- or is emailing them for permission surrendering the sea?
